html:
SMTO-EXE-0097 — SMTO couldn't save the screenshot

GUID: 7781f5f3-d638-5585-a3fe-f62f833f63f4
Slug: screen-artifact-failure
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: screen

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't store the screenshot with the task's files on the Gateway's computer, so it threw the picture away. This usually means the disk there is full or can't be written to.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the computer running the Gateway, check there is free disk space, and delete files you no longer need if it is nearly full. The screenshot is saved on that computer's disk before SMTO can attach it.
  2. Make sure the folder where the Gateway keeps task files hasn't been made read-only or moved. SMTO needs to write the picture there; if it can't, it discards it.
  3. Ask for the screenshot from a chat in SMTO, or start a New chat and ask again. Every screenshot must belong to a chat and task, so a request from outside one can't be saved.

What success looks like

  • The screenshot appears attached to the task in your chat.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it to the person who manages that Gateway. Don't delete other tasks' files to make room unless you know they're no longer needed.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Screenshot publication failed: the request had no owning conversation and run, or atomically writing the image into the Gateway's run artifact workspace failed.

What this means

  • Screenshot publication lacked run/conversation ownership or failed during creation and atomic publication in the Gateway artifact workspace. Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.

Why this can happen

  • Screenshot publication lacked run/conversation ownership or failed during creation and atomic publication in the Gateway artifact workspace.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect artifact scope and retained publication failure, including access or storage facts when available; do not assume the capture itself failed.

How to fix it

  • ScreenService._publish writes a uniquely named screen-.png or screen-.jpeg file atomically under the run artifact workspace (OF_RUN_ARTIFACT_DIR); it also fails if the request lacks conversation_id or run_id. Check that the Gateway's artifact root is writable and has free space, using the existing artifact tools, and make the capture from an active conversation and run.
  • Execute in an active conversation and run. Verify the selected Gateway artifact workspace is writable and has free space; use existing artifact tools to inspect it.

Retry and execution caution

  • Execute in an active conversation and run. Verify the selected Gateway artifact workspace is writable and has free space; use existing artifact tools to inspect it.

How to verify the fix

  • The explicit capture produces a valid artifact attached to its owning run.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass OS permissions, capture another Gateway, or copy screen content to diagnostics.

Technical notes

  • Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
